content.text: Root cause: `to_cents` truncates a binary float — `19.99 * 100` is `1998.9999999999998`, so `int()` gives `1998`. Rounding to the nearest cent fixes it at the source.

content.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `ledger/currency.py`, not in the totals code. `to_cents` used `int(amount * 100)`, which cuts off the decimal part instead of rounding. Prices can't be stored exactly as floats, so `19.99 * 100` comes out as `1998.9999999999998` and `int()` turned it into `1998`. The same thing happened with `4.35`, which became `434` cents per unit and threw off the discount test.

The fix is one line: `return round(amount * 100)`, which rounds to the nearest cent. Every line price goes through this function, so subtotals, discounts, tax and `report.render` all get the right numbers now.

The full test suite passes (5 tests).
